verifications.claim: Submitting Form 4868 by April 15 provides an automatic six-month extension until October 15 to file.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'automatic six-month extension of time to file... postmarked no later than April 15... ends on October 15'; R2: 'Form 4868 automatically grants a six‑month extension, moving the filing deadline to October 15, as long as it is submitted by April 15'; R5: 'extension to file... until Oct. 15... request the extension by April 15'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple IRS sources directly confirm automatic six-month extension to October 15 when Form 4868 is submitted by April 15.

verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'pay any taxes they owe by the April 15 deadline to avoid possible penalties and interest'; R2: 'Any unpaid balance after April 15 may accrue penalties and interest, even if the extension is approved'; R5: 'Taxes owed are still due by April 15. To avoid or minimize penalties and interest'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state interest accrues on unpaid taxes despite the filing extension.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'eliminates the late filing penalties... still required to pay them by the deadline or they could get a financial penalty'; R1: 'pay any taxes they owe... to avoid possible penalties and interest'; R5: 'extra time to file, not additional time to pay'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm extension avoids filing penalty but not payment penalties or interest.

verifications.claim: The extension is to file, not to pay taxes due.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'An extension of time to file a return is not an extension of time to pay'; R2: 'the extension applies only to filing the return, not to paying taxes owed'; R3: 'An extension to file is not an extension to pay'; R5: 'An extension provides extra time to file, not additional time to pay'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated repeatedly in IRS sources.

verifications.claim: IRS Free File allows electronic filing of Form 4868 for free regardless of income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'use IRS Free File to e-file a free extension request'; R2: 'IRS allows anyone, regardless of income, to file an extension for free using its Free File system'; R3: 'Individual taxpayers, regardless of income, can use Free File to electronically request an automatic tax-filing extension'; R5: 'All individual filers can use IRS Free File... at no cost'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly confirmed regardless of income in multiple IRS sources.

verifications.claim: Paying all or part of estimated income tax due using Direct Pay, a debit/credit card, or the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) and selecting "Extension" as the reason results in the IRS automatically processing the extension without filing Form 4868.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'automatically process an extension... using Direct Pay, the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System, or a credit or debit card... won't have to file form 4868'; R2: 'payment through IRS Direct Pay, debit or credit card... indicate that the payment is for an extension. In that case, a separate Form 4868 is not required'; R3, R5 similar.
verifications.reasoning: Precisely matches IRS descriptions of electronic payment options triggering automatic extension.

verifications.claim: Most tax software providers (e.g., TurboTax, H&R Block) offer free federal extension filing.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Most tax software programs and IRS‑authorized e‑file providers allow taxpayers to submit Form 4868 online... Some commercial e‑file providers charge fees... IRS Free File partners... remain free'
verifications.reasoning: R2 supports that most allow submission but notes some charge fees; implies many (e.g., Free File partners) are free, but not explicitly 'most offer free'.

verifications.claim: Paper Form 4868 must be postmarked by April 15.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'postmarked no later than April 15'; R7: 'filing via paper... postmark... April 15'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated for paper filing deadline.

verifications.claim: Taxes owed must be paid by April 15 to avoid penalties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'pay any taxes they owe by the April 15 deadline to avoid possible penalties'; R2: 'pay them by the deadline or they could get a financial penalty'; R5: 'Taxes owed are still due by April 15'

verifications.claim: Late filing penalties can be up to 5% of the unpaid tax per month.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'late filing penalty of 5% of the amount due for every month or part of the month'; R7: 'The penalty is 5% of your unpaid taxes for each month that a return is late'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on late filing penalty rate.

verifications.claim: Late payment penalties are generally 0.5% per month.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention late payment penalties exist and are less than filing penalties but do not specify the 0.5% rate.

verifications.claim: Late payment penalties have a maximum of 25%.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: 25% maximum mentioned only for late filing penalties, not payment.

verifications.claim: Victims of certain natural disasters may receive automatic extensions without filing Form 4868.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Taxpayers in certain federally declared disaster areas'; R5: 'Taxpayers in certain federally declared disaster areas may receive additional time... do not need to request an extension'; R7: 'grants you an automatic extension'

verifications.claim: Automatic extensions for victims of certain natural disasters are listed on the IRS disaster relief page.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Information on the most recent tax relief for disaster situations is available on IRS.gov/disaster'; R7: 'The IRS keeps an official list online of all disaster locations... here'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm IRS page lists disaster relief extensions.

verifications.claim: A federal extension does not automatically extend the state tax deadline.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No source explicitly states that federal extension does not auto-extend state deadlines; R6 shows separate state process but not the direct claim.
